slot_note: re-root after the platform landed architecture 2 (both runs on the golden); one architecture per world, so a new world (a buried-valley aquifer in Indiana), dataset (aquifer-test loggers and a 2005 to 2026 water-level record) and shell (docx and xlsx, a which-question)
niche: a city utility's groundwater withdrawal permit under a conservancy district rule capping the drawdown at a sentinel well through a twenty-year term: which of four requested pumping rates for a new well field in a buried-valley aquifer keeps the 2046 drawdown within the limit (Sulfur task type: inverse problems, physical-model calibration and uncertainty propagation)
answer: File the 1,000 gpm schedule: its greatest monthly drawdown at OW-S in 2046 is 8 ft against the 9 ft limit, where 1,250 gpm reaches 10 ft.
analyst_test: A strong analyst compensates the loggers, fits Theis to the test (an excellent fit), sees its hindcast overshoot the Mill Street record, recalibrates a leaky aquifer against CV-07 or the wells' own baselines and files 1,250 gpm, every rate under 3.5 ft at OW-S.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is a 20-year drawdown forecast at a sentinel well, worked the way hydrogeology works it: aquifer properties from a pumping test, a conceptual model of the far field (walls, leakage) that the test cannot see, and its calibration against the drawdown an existing well field has already caused, separated from the aquifer's natural rise and fall; swap the nouns and there is no confined aquifer, no leakage through till and no cone of depression for a reference well to sit in.
layer1: two logger brands on two clocks (local EDT and UTC), absolute pressure needing the barologger
an observation-well logger re-hung deeper after a download, a logger rewriting its last records
the aquifer's barometric response and earth tides in the minute record
the operating reports in thousand gallons then gallons, the wells renamed at a SCADA change, a meter replacement month estimated from run hours
monitoring readings taken with the nearby well running, a measuring point raised by a casing extension and another cut down
network readings keyed twice, estimated readings, months with no field run
stakeholder_role: Harlow Springs Utilities' water division manager, filing the Reidel Road application

spine.grain: well x minute (test); well x month (record)

world.geography: United States, Indiana (the Corrin Valley, a fictional buried bedrock valley; Harlow Springs, a fictional city)
world.org_type: a city water utility and a regional water conservancy district

driver: The decisive quantity is a long-horizon response to a sustained load, when a short trial's response carries two opposing far-field effects that cancel inside its window and part only over years: the trial's own model fits it closely and overstates the long response, so the far field must be calibrated on the record a nearby load has already left, read against a natural baseline from references beyond that load's reach, because the nearest reference sits inside it and a fitted trend absorbs the response.
driver_concrete: Each requested rate's greatest monthly drawdown at OW-S in 2046 from a bounded leaky aquifer whose leakage factor is calibrated on the drawdown the Mill Street wells caused at MS-MW and OW-S from 2009 to 2026, each well's natural level carried from the far network wells CV-02 and CV-11; not the 72-hour test's Theis fit extrapolated, and not a calibration against the readings' own pre-pumping levels, the nearest network well CV-07 (inside the Mill Street cone) or a fitted trend, each of which credits the region's wet years to leakage.
stump: A strong analyst who sees the test's Theis forecast overshoot the Mill Street record recalibrates the leakage against the nearest network well CV-07 (or the wells' own pre-pumping levels, or a fitted trend) and files 1,250 gpm, every schedule under 3.5 ft at OW-S; only the natural level carried from CV-02 and CV-11 beyond the cone files 1,000 gpm.
deep_chain: (1) the test's Theis fit is exact but blind to the far field, shown by its hindcast of the Mill Street record; (2) the record's drawdown is the reading's fall below its natural level, and the natural level must come from confined-aquifer wells beyond the cone (CV-02, CV-11), not CV-07 or a trend; (3) the leakage factor calibrated on that drawdown with the plate's walls; (4) the 2027 to 2046 superposition at OW-S under each schedule and the town's projection
judgment: which reference wells carry the natural level (CV-07's record steps down with each Mill Street increase and cycles with the summer pumping, CV-02 and CV-11 agree with each other and with OW-S before 2009), and the far-field model that reproduces the separated drawdown out of the test's window
one_fact_test: 'the aquifer leaks' rescues nothing: the leakage must be calibrated, and on the raw or CV-07-referenced record it calibrates to 1,300 gpm

differentiation.mark308: mark308 v1 rebuilds unmet requests the record never stored from supply movements; here every reading is stored and the decisive step is which reference wells carry the aquifer's natural level, so the far field calibrated on an existing cone is not credited with the region's wet years
differentiation.mark166: mark166 v3 forecasts next year's arrivals through departures linked across groups; here nothing arrives or departs: a sustained pumping response is calibrated on an existing well field's cone against natural levels from reference wells outside it
differentiation.mark247: mark247 rebuilds a running sum from a record whose gaps were filled by decay toward normal; here no record is filled: the natural level is carried from reference wells beyond the cone because the nearest one sits inside it

lineage.driver: The extra input an upgraded service level puts into a unit is the part of the unit the old level left untreated, so the average gain measured on units upgraded earlier, chosen because the old level already treated much of them, understates the gain for units the old level barely reached, while their upgraded level less the new units' present input overstates it; only the gain conditioned on how much of each unit the old level already treated, read from each unit's own record under it, carries across to the new units.
lineage.stump: A competent solver takes the Priority 1 collectors' salt per lane-km per severity point less the 424 lane-km's own Priority 2 salt and files 2,600 t at the planning severity, or takes the before-and-after gain of the collectors moved to Priority 1 since 2022 and files 1,500 to 1,600 t; the step that lands it there is carrying an average across streets whose Priority 2 coverage differs, when the gain is the length Priority 2 left untreated and the earlier moves were mostly hill, school and inner-suburb streets Priority 2 had already salted along much of their length, so only the gain conditioned on each street's own Priority 2 salt files 2,200 t.
lineage.driver_concrete: Quellbrook's Priority 2 trucks salt a collector only at its intersections, hills and curves, so a collector's gain on moving to Priority 1 is mostly the stretch between them at the Priority 1 rate; the collectors moved from 2022 to 2025 were mostly hill, school and hospital-access streets whose Priority 2 salt already covered much of their length, while the redesign's 424 lane-km are long flat outer-suburb grid collectors whose Priority 2 trucks salted about a sixth of them, so the moved streets' average gain understates theirs and the Priority 1 collectors' rate less the new streets' own Priority 2 salt overstates it; only the gain read off each moved street's own Priority 2 salt, at the new streets' Priority 2 salt, carries across.
lineage.fate: landed on the portal (2026-11-07): one response filed the golden 2,200 t by regressing each earlier move's gain on its own Priority 2 salt and reading it at the new streets' (100 per cent), the other filed the default 2,600 t and still kept 70 per cent on the asks; conditioning a carried gain on a covariate each unit's history prints is the strong solver's reflex, so the world is spent
spent 2026-11-08 on the platform: both runs bounded the tank's dewatering by the Southside plant's hourly headroom and landed Alternative C and every ask (REDESIGN)
lineage.driver: A storage buffer that captures a discharge until it is full empties only through a receiving channel whose spare capacity vanishes for one to several days after each wet event, so in a run of events the buffer meets the next one still partly full; counting each event against an empty buffer, or a buffer emptied at its outlet's rated pace, understates how often it spills, and only replaying the record with the outlet bounded by the receiving channel's spare capacity, read from that channel's own record, prices the size the limit needs.
lineage.driver_concrete: Clay Street's tank is pumped out into the Southside interceptor at the plant headworks, and the Southside plant, its sewershed full of groundwater and inflow, takes its 140 MGD hydraulic limit for one to four days after most storms from March to June; the Northside tank, whose plant has room within hours, empties at its pumps' rating and its overflows replay exactly that way, but Clay Street's pumps can only send what Southside has room for, so in a wet spell the tank meets the next storm still full and the 26 MG alternative that clears four events at its pumps' rating leaves 6.8 a year; only the 38 MG tank, at 2.9, meets the decree.
lineage.stump: A competent solver replays Outfall 014's metered overflows through each tank pumped out at its station's rated dewatering flow (the continuous simulation the decree evaluates by, which reproduces the Northside tank's overflows since 2020) and selects Alternative B, the 26 MG tank, at 2.8 events a year; the step that lands it there is taking the pumps' rating as the pace the tank empties, when it empties into the Southside interceptor at the headworks of a plant that sits at its 140 MGD limit for days after wet-season storms, so only a replay bounded by Southside's own headroom hour by hour shows the 20 MG tank at 6.8 events and selects Alternative C, the 38 MG tank, at 2.9.
lineage.answer: Select Alternative C, the 38 MG tank: it leaves Outfall 014 2.9 untreated overflow events a year, where the 26 MG Alternative B leaves 6.8.
